name: R3.21 Rust CI and unchanged watcher-probe wake-up repair
objective: Repair all terminal R3.20 exact-SHA CI failures in one bounded milestone: restore Rust CI compilation/formatting and make the unchanged watcher-probe request reach the idle OpenObsidian UI on Linux, macOS, and Windows without changing reconciliation behavior or weakening assertions.
scope: In crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs, add the explicit VaultWatchEventBatch element type to target_batches to resolve E0282, and apply only the six rustfmt hunks reported by the R3.20 Ubuntu CI log.

In the round-trip CI harness, after atomically writing the unchanged-probe request marker, dispatch two distinct harmless platform-native pointer-move events inside the OpenObsidian client window (neutral point, then wake point) so a fresh UI frame reads the marker. Send no pointer button events and make no vault or app-data edits.

Record the wake event platform, window/client coordinates, visibility/foreground receipt where available, and zero button events in the round-trip report; the exact request-correlated watcher-rescan log entry and subsequent unchanged probe remain the proof that the app consumed the request.

Clarify the milestone-only submission cadence in goal.md and synchronize its fingerprint in requirements/state. Update migration state, journal, and evidence locally with R3.20 terminal job/artifact reconciliation and the complete R3.21 plan/review/implementation status.
out_of_scope: Changing watcher production behavior, notification policy, request correlation, batch lineage, or the 60-second reconciliation timer.
Adding a polling timer, forcing manual refresh, extending the existing probe timeout, changing the unchanged-snapshot/no-refresh conditions, or weakening callback/refresh correlation.
Changing unrelated watcher tests, app behavior, feature requirements, compatibility claims, workflows, or artifact policy.
Running local tests, builds, formatters, linters, validators, runtime probes, benchmarks, or application launches as acceptance.
implementation_criteria: The `target_batches` inference failure is fixed by an explicit Vec<VaultWatchEventBatch> type and the source diff contains only the six CI-reported formatter hunks in that watcher test block.

The unchanged-probe harness writes its existing request marker, then dispatches two distinct native pointer-move events to safe coordinates inside the visible target window. Linux uses motion-only xdotool commands; macOS posts only CGEventType.mouseMoved; Windows verifies OpenObsidian is visible/foreground, SetCursorPos succeeds, and GetCursorPos matches each requested client-area point. No button-down/up API is called.

The app consumes the marker in a UI update frame, requests the existing watcher rescan and a repaint, then observes the watcher callback/probe on the current or a subsequent frame. Require the exact request ID through the watcher-rescan log, watcher hint, and unchanged probe; do not require the full chain in one frame.
The 60-second periodic reconciliation timer, 30-second helper timeout, and all strict no-refresh assertions stay unchanged; the wake produces no vault or app-data edits.
Bound native wake helper invocations with command timeouts. Report platform visibility/foreground only when actually measured; use null for those fields on macOS until the harness can verify them.

The goal and requirements tracker record the same milestone-only cadence and current goal fingerprint: minor edits stay local; one complete, reviewed milestone is pushed once; origin/main remains at that submitted SHA throughout the potentially multi-hour required CI batch.
The complete source and tracker diff is independently reviewed as one milestone before submission; no local executable validation is used.
ci_acceptance: Every required job passes on the same submitted SHA, including Rust CI on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Rust 1.95.

Linux, macOS, and Windows each record the unchanged-probe request ID, a motion-only wake with distinct coordinates, the app consuming the marker, a watcher hint before its scheduled probe, an unchanged result equal to the baseline full-vault revision, and a quiet interval without a correlated full refresh.

The report records zero pointer button events and the watcher diagnostics continue to show timer_due_before_poll=false; on Windows the request is sent only after visibility/foreground and cursor-position checks pass.
All existing later note edit, rename, persistence, reopen, and quiet-window round-trip scenarios pass unchanged.
All required exact-SHA artifacts are enumerated and reconciled by workflow/run/SHA, API size/digest, and payload identity using the metadata-only policy for large desktop previews.
submission_gate: Keep R3.21 local until the bounded implementation is complete and independently reviewed as a whole. Immediately before submission, verify origin/main still equals a0049c751d82540a9eca12e5323c05c673beacf9 and R3.20 has all jobs and artifacts terminal/reconciled. Then fast-forward the reviewed milestone to origin/main exactly once. Hold main at the submitted SHA until all seven workflows, all jobs, and artifacts are reconciled; do not push minor edits or status-only updates.
implementation_review_status: Approved as a complete milestone by r320_integrated_review, r320_roundtrip_repair_analysis, and a590_attempt3_rust_ci; ready for one push after exact-base/no-active-batch preflight.
next_action: Pass the exact-base/no-active-batch preflight, commit the reviewed milestone locally, and push it once to origin/main. Then hold main at the submitted SHA until all required workflows, jobs, and artifacts are terminal and reconciled.
